parties:
Alauddin ------ Petitioner
Vs.
The State ------ Respondents
full_judgment: 7. As it appears, regarding confessional statement, the High Court Division held that the confessional statement was an inculpatory one wherein the petitioner not only stated that he murdered his wife by throttling but also stated some events of their conjugal life in the fateful night which could not be tutored to him and the Magistrate in his evidence in unequivocal terms also stated that he recorded the confessional statement of the accused after observing all legal formalities and the confessional statement was also voluntary, the principle laid down in 17 BLD 352 is not applicable in the facts and circumstances of the present case as there is no interpolation in the confessional statement made by the petitioner and all the columns of the printed form were filled up by the recording Magistrate.
